directPlan.targetTier: T1 where the actual boundary is exercised
requiredEvidence: mixed-age/shared-reference media claims and forced storage failure
stale job/X owner rejection, generation rotation, checked zero-row writes, and provider-start ambiguity
disposable PostgreSQL replay, no network, and exact cleanup receipt

supersession.effect: This new receipt supplies the later successful local/disposable T1 evidence. The blocked predecessor remains unchanged and valid as the record of the earlier failed attempt.

b2b.supersession: E6 addresses the prior REWORK and adds the missing disposable PostgreSQL and application-boundary evidence without rewriting the old receipt.

b3a.supersession: E6 adds current disposable runtime acceptance and the ambiguity-history repairs without rewriting the old receipt.

ledger.mutation: No ledger row was appended or changed while this receipt was authored. A separately reviewed append-only row may bind this receipt later.

protectedOriginals.state: byte-exact unchanged; the intentional missing final newline is preserved

forwardOnlySuccessors.purpose: repair the B2B deletion token type to uuid
repair expired-job reconciliation while preserving fenced ownership
replace an untyped all-NULL CASE with a typed-safe direct NULL assignment
prevent force retry of an ambiguous latest receipt
make the ambiguity/provider-start guard history-wide while retaining ordinary pre-provider force retry

b2b: Mixed-age media-object claims retain shared references and delete only rows owned by the current deletion token.
A forced storage failure is exercised through the application boundary and does not clear database references.
The disposable PostgreSQL fixture executes the real current RPC surface and validates the uuid deletion-token repair.
b3a: Stale job and X owners/generations are rejected by checked zero-row writes.
Generation rotation displaces stale owners without allowing an old generation to complete or fail the claim.
A rejected provider-start marker permits zero provider calls at the application boundary.
Provider acceptance followed by completion-write uncertainty is reported as ambiguous/non-success, never success.
Any non-posted receipt history with claim_state ambiguous or provider_started_at non-null blocks force retry until explicit reconciliation, even when a newer ordinary failed row exists.
An ordinary failed/skipped receipt created before provider start remains force-retryable.
securitySurface: Successor function bodies retain SECURITY DEFINER, closed search_path, and service-role-only grants in the disposable replay.
No production ownership, production grant, or production type-equivalence claim is made.

rootCauseAndRepairTrail.finding: The accepted fail_x_post_delivery body used claim_expires_at = CASE WHEN v_ambiguous THEN NULL ELSE NULL END; PostgreSQL resolved the all-NULL CASE as text and rejected assignment to timestamptz.
rootCauseAndRepairTrail.repair: The 1530 successor uses a direct NULL assignment without modifying the protected original.

rootCauseAndRepairTrail.finding: force_retry could reclaim an ambiguous failed receipt.
rootCauseAndRepairTrail.repair: The 1630 successor added an ambiguity gate before the force-retry path.

rootCauseAndRepairTrail.finding: provider_started_at can be non-null while claim_state is failed when the caller supplies a skip reason, and a newer ordinary receipt could mask older provider-started or ambiguous history.
rootCauseAndRepairTrail.repair: The 1730 successor makes the guard history-wide over every non-posted receipt with claim_state ambiguous or provider_started_at non-null, while preserving ordinary pre-provider retry.

rootCauseAndRepairTrail.finding: The earlier 121-migration replay allowed Deno to emit Download lines.
rootCauseAndRepairTrail.repair: The runner and checker now require npm --offline plus Deno --cached-only --frozen --deny-net in exact order. The final 122-migration run emitted no Download line and is the only accepted replay.
